_meta.recallFanoutRemoved: **Corrected 2026-10-05.** `recall.fanout` was removed from this file, from `C0` and `C2`, and from the policy itself (`packages/core/src/types.ts`, `AssemblyPolicy.recall`; `packages/core/src/config.ts`, `LEGACY_POLICY_KEYS`). It was `k`, the per-node expansion fanout of the recall walk - each BFS node expanded at most its k heaviest neighbours - and the line this file carried read `"fanout": 8`. It is gone because it was **never in the originating brief** (the prompt mentions it zero times; the brief bounds recall with `recall.depth` and `recall.threshold` only, plus `recall.window`, which it says exists only to save System-1 calls and must not affect recall), **in no record** (the tape's `kind:"wiring"` record carries `recall: {d, r, w, wait, tier1}` and no k, and the round manifests do not name it), and **in no panel** (the plugin's `Tuning` fields are depth, relevanceThreshold, window, anchorWaitMs and tracePlacement) - so a parameter that decided behaviour lived only in the presets, and `C2.json`'s own `provider` note says the wiring record, not the preset, is the authority. **This cell ran the cap with recall selection off** (`recall.tier1: 'off'`), so the walk never ran in it and the field could not have decided anything here; what the round recorded is the point below. **What the round it was measured in recorded: no number of that round changes with the removal.** In `round-20261004-1239` the walk returned `candidates = 0` from invocation 9 onward, because the System-1 lane was 4.6x too slow to score the pairs and the tail therefore had no edges, so `fanout` had no effect on anything that round wrote. The rounds that did record a non-empty walk (`20261004-0233`, `20261004-1211`) stay readable and unedited: the field is gone from the policy, and a preset or profile that still writes it is read and reported rather than dropped in silence. **What replaced it:** `recall.threshold`, the brief's own knob and the one that is in the settings panel. The trade is recorded in `packages/core/src/types.ts`: on the 36.8 % of anchors where the cap did bite, the uncapped walk selects more segments (median +27, worst +69), and lowering `r` is how a round asks for a smaller block.
_meta.note: **Corrected 2026-10-05, and the superseded wording is carried here because this note is a record.** It read: "The state proxy T is delivered and the current task x sits before the recalled block, not after it: `xFirst: true` and `deliver: true` both come from `cellPolicy('C1')` (packages/core/src/types.ts) and are not repeated here, because a value in this file would silently override the cell." `xFirst` no longer exists, and neither does the question's position it was renamed to: `questionPlacement` ('first'/'last') lived for one day and was **deleted** on 2026-10-05 (the paper fixes the question last in every condition, and `'first'` produced `[T, q, x]`, neither paper arm), so `q` is the last block of every recorded order by construction. `tracePlacement` ('trace-as-state'/'trace-append') is the arm - whether T is in front of the long context or behind it - code-owned and absent from this file, and an old profile spelling is still read and reported (`LEGACY_LAYOUT_KEYS`, packages/core/src/config.ts): question-last spellings are warned about as retired and harmless, question-first ones are refused with the sentence that retired them. **Why the rename:** the paper places the question last in every condition (arXiv:2609.02702 section 4.1) and its two arms are `[T, x, q]` (Trace as State) and `[x, T, q]` (Trace Append) with order the only difference - `xFirst` moved the question, the one element the paper fixes, and its name presented that as the paper's variable. **Evidence:** round `20261004-0233`'s own `layoutOrder` records - this cell recorded `pinned, stateProxy, anchor, recalled, tail`, the question second, which is neither paper arm, while `C0` recorded `pinned, recalled, tail, anchor`. What is true of the delivered text is a property of the insertion channel rather than of a layout field: T is delivered and the recalled turns follow it, so the model reads `[..., x, T, recalled, ...]` in every delivering cell whatever the recorded order says. `deliver: true` comes from `cellPolicy('C1')` (packages/core/src/types.ts) and is not repeated here, because a value in this file would silently override the cell. **Registration changed 2026-10-04**: `deliver` was `false` from 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-03, and the arm was a second control delivering nothing until the delivery channel began sending T - see `_meta.secondControl`. The registered contrasts are now `C0 -> C1` (what the trace's presence buys, lane absent) and `C1 -> C2` (what recall selection buys on top); the endpoint test in docs/FORMULAS.md §8 is still C0 against C2, and the statement of record is the comment above `cellPolicy()`. **What has NOT changed and is still not measurable**: the paper's variable is the trace's POSITION (Trace as State `M([T, x, q])` against Trace Append `M([x, T, q])`), and delivery appends - it renders T before the recalled block by construction, whatever `policy.tracePlacement` says - and since 2026-10-05 that field is the enforced axis naming the paper's two orders, where the old `stateProxyPosition` composed with a boolean `xFirst` that moved the question instead - so no arm presents the trace after the context and the position axis reaches the recorded `layout.order`, not the delivered text. The following is kept as the record it is: in round 20261001-1300 the TAS-alone arm (then labelled `C2`) measured 14 441 tokens per step against the baseline's 21 054 (about 0.69x), of which 1 783 were uncached input tokens per step against 2 595 (also about 0.69x) with 1 493 output tokens against 1 523. **That figure is not a contrast this arm could support, and never was**: that round's own control plane holds 13 `context_delivery` records for this arm and `delivered: false` on every one of them, with 0 of 13 assemblies carrying a non-empty recalled block, while the baseline arm was refused by policy ("policy.deliver is off: the cell leaves context to the harness") on all 19 - so the 21 054-against-14 441 difference was measured between two arms whose model-visible input differed by nothing. The quantities are per step because the cells' absolute totals are not comparable: they ran a different number of steps. **Corrected 2026-10-05 (the recalled block's position - appended, because this note is a record).** The recalled block now sits immediately before the anchor, behind the tail, in both orders this build lays out; it used to be third of five, with `tail` and `anchor` behind it. That is a move *inside* the paper's long context `x`, not a move of the paper's variable: the variable is where `T` sits relative to `x`, and this cell's arm is unchanged, because `T` is still ahead of every block of `x` under `trace-as-state`. The block order is the table in `packages/core/src/assembler.ts`'s header and `AssemblyLayout.order` (`packages/core/src/types.ts`) is the statement of record; neither is restated as a rule here. What this note records about the delivered text did not change with the move: `T` is still rendered before the recalled turns by construction, so the model still reads `[..., x, T, recalled, ...]` in this cell - where a block sits inside `x` reaches the recorded `layout.order` and the cache arithmetic, not the insertion channel. **Why it moved:** prompt caching is prefix caching, so anything placed behind a block that changes every step is invalidated with it, and the recalled block is the block a re-selection moves. Measured on round `20261004-1458` C2: the whole-prompt invalidation span per delivered pair fell from 2,539 to 2,111 tokens with this move, on top of the ordering change that had already cut it from 6,179 to 2,539. The round record quoted above (round `20261004-0233` recorded this cell's order) is that round's own data and is left as written, and no value in this file changed with any of this.
_meta.secondControl: **HISTORICAL, and superseded on 2026-10-04 - the key name is kept so the record stays readable.** This arm was carried as a second control arm from 2026-10-02: `deliver` was `true` until then and could never fire, and when it was set to `false` the registration became C0 against C2. The reason that was correct at the time, kept verbatim because it is the reason the arm was closed: `deliverContext` could insert exactly one block, `recalled` - the state proxy T was deliberately never sent (packages/dsh-plugin/src/context-delivery.ts) - and with `recall.tier1: 'off'` that block is empty by construction, because the BFS walk, the unjudged fail-open and the recency fallback all sit behind one guard (`policy.recall.tier1 !== 'off' && recalledBudget > 0`, packages/core/src/assembler.ts - **that guard is quoted as it stood when the arm was closed; its second conjunct went with the recall token cap, retired 2026-10-05, so the guard that runs is `policy.recall.tier1 !== 'off'` alone and `recalledBudget` no longer exists**). Both recorded rounds agreed. Round `20261002-2037`: 76 assemblies, **0** with `blocks.recalled > 0`, and on the only two steps whose decision carried any messages the refusal was literally "nothing to insert: relevance selected no turns" (the other 74 were "the decision carried no messages"). Round `20261001-1300`: 13 assemblies, 13 refusals, **0** `delivered: true`, 0 with a non-empty recalled block. **Re-opened 2026-10-04 because every fact that closed it stopped being true**: the delivery channel now sends T, so with `tier1: 'off'` this arm has exactly the thing the method is about - the trace alone - and that is a delivery rather than an empty refusal. `cellPolicy('C1')` sets `deliver: true` again. What survives unchanged from the closure argument is the part that is about the *other* half of TAS: the model-view write-back (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; `packages/proxy` does not exist) is still what it was - it has to deliver a *layout* rather than one appended block - so the POSITION of T is still unmeasurable in any arm. This arm is a control over recall selection and over the lane, not over the layout.
_meta.providerNone: `s1.provider: none` because this arm is a no-System-1 control: `recall.tier1: 'off'` disables recall *selection* but association-graph upkeep is not gated on it, so without this key the arm still scores pairs and reports System-1 calls - 257 of them in round 20261001-1300 - and the TAS half is a claim about ordering, which must be measurable with the System-1 lane absent rather than merely unscoped, reporting zero System-1 calls, tokens and time. Run recipe: a live profile must pair `s1.provider: none` with `laya.enabled: false`, because `laya.enabled: true` beside `provider: none` is a reported conflict (`singleBackendIssues`, packages/s1-client/src/resolve.ts); `laya` is a profile key and is deliberately not carried by this preset.
